data.title: FP8 is ~100 tflops faster when the kernel name has "cutlass" in it
data.author: limoce
data.article_summary: 文章提到，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能导致在x.com网站上出现问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过这个方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA的`libnvidia-nvvm.so`库中与`cutlass`相关的优化行为是否合理，是否属于作弊或不正当的性能提升。

不同观点：
• [hvenev] 认为`cutlass`可能是一种优化属性，允许编译器对内核行为做出一般情况下不成立的假设，从而实现性能提升。
• [spoaceman7777] 指出，这种变化可能是由于NVIDIA和CUTLASS项目中正在进行的FP8支持工作，并且最近由外部贡献者添加了替代代码路径，而不是通过自定义内部CUDA构建来实现的。并提供了一个相关的GitHub链接（NVIDIA/cutlass#2037）来支持这一观点。
• [tempaway43563] 询问CUTLASS是什么，并质疑通过检查内核名称来进行优化是否合理或属于作弊行为，提供了CUTLASS的文档链接以供参考。
• [high_na_euv] 基于对编译器和LLVM的经验，解释说许多复杂的过程依赖于名称解析，包括类型名称等，因此这种情况可能是无意中发生的，而非恶意行为。
• [giingyui] 质疑使用该内核名称优化的缺点，认为不仅仅是加速，除非其中包含大量的sleep(x)调用。
• [rowanG077] 希望这只是一个对内部内核有效的无辜优化，不能普遍应用。
• [zahlman] 认为有人断章取义，误解了原始材料，指出在某些内核上使用FP8比FP16有更好的性能表现，但否认这是作弊行为，并批评这种解读。

补充讨论：
• [KomoD] 提供了相关的GitHub链接，指向Triton项目的具体pull request（#7298）。
• [PLenz] 提到了大众排放测试模型，但并未深入讨论。
• [koakuma-chan] 询问100 TFLOS是否算很多，与主要讨论点关系不大。
• [Arch-TK] 抱怨人们不正确使用Git，但未直接参与核心讨论。
• [orlp] 提到了"GenuineIntel moment"，但没有展开。
• [nolok] 提到了Intel在信任和检查上的问题，但与主要讨论点关系较小。

争议焦点：
• 使用内核名称`cutlass`作为优化依据是否属于作弊行为，还是只是一种合理的性能优化手段。
• 这种优化是否无意中发生的，还是有意为之。
• 这种优化是否可以普遍应用，或仅限于特定内核。

GhidrAssistMCP
A powerful Ghidra extension that provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, enabling AI assistants and other tools to interact with Ghidra's reverse engineering capabilities through a standardized API.
Overview
GhidrAssistMCP bridges the gap between AI-powered analysis tools and Ghidra's comprehensive reverse engineering platform. By implementing the Model Context Protocol, this extension allows external AI assistants, automated analysis tools, and custom scripts to seamlessly interact with Ghidra's analysis capabilities.
Key Features
** MCP Server Integration**: Full Model Context Protocol server implementation using official SDK
** 31 Built-in Tools**: Comprehensive set of analysis tools covering functions, data, cross-references, and more
** Configurable UI**: Easy-to-use interface for managing tools and monitoring activity
** Real-time Logging**: Track all MCP requests and responses with detailed logging
** Dynamic Tool Management**: Enable/disable tools individually with persistent settings
** Current Context Awareness**: Tools that understand Ghidra's current cursor position and active function

data.title: Exposing a web service with Cloudflare Tunnel (2022)
data.author: sturza
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Cloudflare Tunnel在不暴露服务器端口的情况下安全地托管web服务。首先，通过安装`cloudflared`客户端并登录Cloudflare账户进行授权。接着，创建一个隧道（tunnel），获取其凭证和ID。然后，建议配置`systemd`服务以更好地管理隧道。具体步骤包括创建配置文件和设置服务，以确保隧道能稳定运行。Cloudflare Tunnel通过在服务器和Cloudflare数据中心之间建立持久的外向连接，保护服务器不被直接暴露在公共互联网中，同时实现正常的应用托管。这种方法适用于各种环境，包括家庭服务器或Kubernetes集群等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare Tunnel 的使用及其安全性、实用性

不同观点：
• **teiferer** 认为使用 Cloudflare Tunnel 与直接开放端口在安全风险上没有本质区别，因为最终处理流量的还是家中的服务器进程。他对 Cloudflare 是否过滤流量以及如何判断好坏流量表示质疑。
• **44za12** 非常喜欢使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，并成功在旧的 Raspberry Pi 上托管了博客和多个项目，展示了实际使用案例。
• **mgerdts** 指出，如果互联网暴露的应用被攻破，攻击者可能会轻松访问家庭网络，因此需要额外的防护措施。
• **yegle** 提到根据 Cloudflare 的服务条款，通过 Cloudflare Tunnel 传输媒体流可能违反规定，他自己选择使用 oauth2-proxy 来保护 Plex 服务。
• **ajd555** 表示自己多年使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，并且免费 tier 非常慷慨，没有遇到任何问题，甚至有 kubernetes 部署方案。
• **agnishom** 询问是否可以用 tailscale funnel 实现同样的功能，暗示对替代方案的兴趣。
• **jz10** 提到在工作中使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，但觉得 web 界面不易用，因此开发了一个 TUI 工具来管理隧道，并增加了基本认证保护。

补充讨论：
• **speerer** 对 Cloudflare 的服务条款表示担忧，特别是其中关于用户内容永久授权给 Cloudflare 的条款。
• **cedws** 询问是否有人用 Cloudflare Tunnel 运行私人邮件服务器，暗示对这种特定用途的兴趣。
• **kramer2718** 对该方案表示赞赏，并计划在即将到来的项目中使用。
• **Hikikomori** 分享了自己使用 Zero Trust 认证保护服务的经验，并提到创建了一个 Python 脚本自动处理相关配置。
• **theyknowitsxmas** 指出现在的设置过程已经简化为从仪表板复制粘贴，并且可以通过 Access 保护子域，提供了简化操作的信息。
• **jekwoooooe** 表示喜欢使用 Cloudflare Tunnel 来暴露内部服务，并通过 Google 认证和其他零信任保护措施来确保安全。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare Tunnel 是否真正提升了安全性，尤其是与直接开放端口相比。
• Cloudflare 服务条款的限制，特别是内容授权条款，是否会对用户造成困扰。

44507799.article_content:
There are lots of ways to host a web service.
You might want to rent a VPS, Dedicated Server, or embrace full serverless and write your application for a service like Cloudflare Workers
You might want to use Docker, k8s, LXD, or any other manner of deploying your services.
You might have a complex setup to proxy and serve traffic through your IP.
But sometimes you might not have it all figured out. You might want to run your service in your home on that one old laptop you have lying around, or you might be worried about forwarding your IP and connections to the world without properly securing them. Setting it all up sounds like a hassle, right?
This is where I believe a hidden gem of Cloudflare comes out to shine.
Cloudflare Tunnel
is an extremely innovative product by Cloudflare to seamlessly protect your web server from ever being directly targeted or exposed, while still allowing you to host your applications like normal.
Ensure your server is safe, no matter where it’s running: public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes cluster, or even a Mac mini under your TV.
~ Cloudflare
Even with the best firewall in the world, you still have machines exposed to the public Internet.
But what if you could host a web service with no ports exposed? Well, you can! Cloudflare Tunnel makes a persistent outbound connection (a tunnel!) between your server and Cloudflare's nearest datacenter. All the traffic to your domain flows through this outgoing tunnel and connects to your server through the protection of Cloudflare. This also has the benefit of being seamlessly encrypted, so you don't have to worry about a thing when it comes to the security of your web service.
If you, like me, think that sounds amazing, read on to get started creating your own tunnel.
Getting started
Note: There is now an easier way to create and manage tunnels through the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard.
You can check out how to do that
on the Cloudflare developer documentation
.
For this walkthrough I will assume you are on a Linux-based operating system. For testing I used Ubuntu 20.04. Some things may vary if you have a different system, though on Debian at least it should be the same.
This walkthrough also assumes that you have a Cloudflare account with a domain on it already, if you don't have one then you should add one and return here!
I also asssume a small level of technical and command-line ability, but it isn't anything overlay daunting so feel free to give it a go regardless! I'm in the comments if you get stuck!
First things first, you'll need to download
cloudflared
, the command-line client for interacting with Cloudflare Tunnels. The
official documentation
is a bit better at explaining this than I am, but for a x86_64 Ubuntu machine you would do the following:
$ wget -q
https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb
$ sudo dpkg -i cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb
Then, you can verify your installation by issuing
cloudflared version
and observing the recent version given!
The wget, dpkg and "cloudflared version" command described above being executed. The dpkg command returns the installation output for cloudflared while "cloudflared version" returns "cloudflared version 2022.2.0 (built 2022-02-04-114 UTC)"
Now that you have the client running, you need to authorize with your Cloudflare account:
$ cloudflared tunnel login
This will give out a URL that you can visit to authorise yourself. While it isn't 100% vital that you select the right domain at this stage, I would recommend choosing one that you would like to try out a tunnel on. You can run the tunnel on any subdomain or domain later down the road.
For this example I picked
erisa.dev
and I am now logged in!
The command "cloudflared tunnel login" being ran. The output is a dash.cloudflare.com URL and afterwards "You have successfully logged in."
After logging yourself in, you can now get started creating tunnels!
$ cloudflared tunnel create mytunnel
You can name it whatever you want, in this case I chose
mytunnel
as my tunnel's name.
After issuing this command you're going to get two important pieces of information: the file path to a .json file containing the tunnels credentials, and an ID for tunnel. In this case I have a tunnel with an ID of
ed5bfe16-cb5f-449c-b2e9-7c300b749c79
and the credentials are stored at
/home/ubuntu/.cloudflared/ed5bfe16-cb5f-449c-b2e9-7c300b749c79.json
.
Keep this information to hand, because you will need it in a minute!
At this point, you could happily go ahead and configure a tunnel with your own user account and run it with
$ cloudflared tunnel run mytunnel
however the best practise would be in setting up a
systemd
service for your tunnel from the beginning. So this is what I will be instructing!
First, we need a directory to store the config:
$ sudo mkdir -p /etc/cloudflared
Then, we can get started creating a configuration file!
The file we're going to create is
/etc/cloudflared/config.yml
and you can use

data.title: Kimi k2 largest open source SOTA model?
data.author: ConteMascetti71
data.article_summary: Kimi K2是Moonshot AI团队开发的先进混合专家（MoE）大语言模型系列，拥有1万亿总参数和320亿激活参数。通过Muon优化器训练，Kimi K2在知识前沿、推理和编码任务中表现优异，并针对工具使用、推理和自主问题解决进行了优化。模型包括Kimi-K2-Base和Kimi-K2-Instruct两个版本，分别适用于研究定制和通用聊天。评估结果显示，Kimi K2在编码、数学、通用任务等多项基准测试中达到或超越了当前最优水平（SOTA），尤其在SWE-bench测试中表现出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kimi K2模型的技术表现、开放性及其应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• Vessenes认为Kimi K2在解决某些编码问题时表现出色，尤其适合在集成应用场景中使用。尽管它需要大量计算资源（约16块H200s），但其风格与其他模型有所不同，整体体验良好。

• Ozgune指出Kimi K2是一个令人印象深刻的通用大语言模型，但由于当前AI前沿已经转向推理和多模态模型，它没有获得足够关注。Ozgune建议如果将Kimi K2用于训练推理模型，可能会产生有趣的结果。

• Satvikpendem对Kimi K2的所谓“开源”提出质疑，指出其“修改版MIT许可证”包含商业使用限制，认为其开放性有限。

• Sagarpatil提到AI模型中普遍存在使用破折号的问题，并指出ChatGPT在明确告知后仍继续使用，质疑模型在格式控制上的问题。

• Exegeist赞扬Kimi K2的非机械化人格表现，认为其在语言风格上接近Anthropic的优秀模型，表现出色。

• Fzysingularity猜测Kimi K2的表现可能导致OpenAI推迟发布其开源模型，因为Kimi K2在某些指标上可能超越了OpenAI的模型。

• Jug认为非推理模型在特定应用场景中仍有价值，尤其在不涉及逻辑难题或STEM主题的情况下，可以作为更经济的选项。

• Emacdona猜测Kimi K2的发布可能导致OpenAI出于安全考虑推迟其新开源模型的发布。

1. Model Introduction
Kimi K2 is a state-of-the-art mixture-of-experts (MoE) language model with 32 billion activated parameters and 1 trillion total parameters. Trained with the Muon optimizer, Kimi K2 achieves exceptional performance across frontier knowledge, reasoning, and coding tasks while being meticulously optimized for agentic capabilities.
Key Features
Large-Scale Training: Pre-trained a 1T parameter MoE model on 15.5T tokens with zero training instability.
MuonClip Optimizer: We apply the Muon optimizer to an unprecedented scale, and develop novel optimization techniques to resolve instabilities while scaling up.
Agentic Intelligence: Specifically designed for tool use, reasoning, and autonomous problem-solving.
Model Variants
Kimi-K2-Base
: The foundation model, a strong start for researchers and builders who want full control for fine-tuning and custom solutions.
Kimi-K2-Instruct
: The post-trained model best for drop-in, general-purpose chat and agentic experiences. It is a reflex-grade model without long thinking.

data.title: Bypassing Google's big anti-adblock update
data.author: deryilz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何发现Google Chrome中一个绕过其反广告拦截更新的漏洞。随着Chrome从MV2转向MV3，谷歌取消了`webRequestBlocking`权限，这严重影响了广告拦截器的功能。作者发现，通过利用Chrome扩展中某些仍使用JavaScript绑定的API，特别是`chrome.webRequest`，可以绕过这一限制。具体而言，作者利用了`chrome.webRequest`事件的构造函数，创建一个带有WebView ID的假事件，从而绕过权限检查，恢复了广告拦截功能。这个漏洞源于Chrome在处理扩展绑定时的安全漏洞，尽管大部分API已改为C++实现，但仍有部分遗留的JS绑定文件存在问题。作者在2023年向Google报告了此漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：谷歌Chrome浏览器对广告拦截器（adblockers）和扩展程序的限制（尤其是通过Manifest V3），以及用户和开发者的应对方式。

不同观点：
• al_borland：认为如果不同意谷歌的做法，正确的做法是放弃Chrome及所有基于Chromium的浏览器，以此打击谷歌的垄断地位，而不是寻找绕过其限制的方法。
• breve：推荐使用Firefox，因为uBlock Origin在Firefox上运行效果最好，可以绕过Chrome中Manifest V3的限制。
• krackers：质疑Manifest V3的安全性，指出谷歌自己承认MV3并不比MV2更安全，这引发对谷歌动机的怀疑。
• SuperShibe：讽刺有人向谷歌报告了绕过MV3限制的方法，导致谷歌修补了该“漏洞”。
• froderick：作为Firefox的长期用户，没有感受到Chrome在广告拦截方面的变化，表示对Chrome用户遭遇的问题表示同情，但无意切换回Chrome。
• throwaway73945：认为有人让谷歌修补了一个无害的“问题”，这个问题本可以被扩展开发者用来绕过MV3的限制，质疑这种行为的价值。
• RockstarSprain：想使用Firefox，但因Firefox不支持PWA（渐进式网络应用）而却步，尽管有第三方扩展可以实现此功能，但出于隐私考虑不愿使用。
• alex1138：批评谷歌试图限制广告拦截器，指出广告有时是恶意或过度追踪的，认为谷歌的行为与公司早期理想主义背道而驰。
• crazygringo：反驳那些认为谷歌为了广告收入而限制广告拦截器的说法，认为uBlock Origin Lite在Chrome上运行良好，且由于过滤在C++中完成，性能更好。
• pnw：推荐使用Brave浏览器，表示自从切换后没有再想念Chrome。
• urda：建议通过安装Firefox来绕过Chrome的限制。
• loloquwowndueo：庆幸只有在工作电脑上使用Chrome，其他地方使用Firefox，并对uBlock Origin在Chrome上的失效表示遗憾。
• daft_pink：询问是否可以通过使用其他基于Chromium的浏览器来避免MV3的限制，并寻求隐私保护的建议。
• bradgessler：建议尝试Safari或Firefox等非Chrome浏览器。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于谷歌通过Manifest V3限制广告拦截器的做法是否合理，以及这是否与谷歌的广告收入模式有关。
• 用户对谷歌的限制措施普遍不满，许多人推荐使用Firefox或其他基于Chromium的浏览器（如Brave）作为替代方案。
• 关于uBlock Origin在Chrome上的运行效果存在不同看法，一部分用户认为影响不大，另一部分用户则对其失效表示失望。
• 有用户指出Firefox在某些功能（如PWA支持）上的不足，这可能是其相较于Chrome的劣势。

44544266.article_content:
D
erin Eryılmaz
How I found a bypass in Google's big anti-adblock update
July 12, 2025
About MV3
If you know anything about browsers, you've probably heard that Google Chrome is phasing out MV2 in favor of MV3. You've probably also heard that this hurts adblockers.
A quick explainer: "MV" stands for "manifest version." MV3 introduces a new type of runtime for Chrome extensions that, among other things, gets rid of
webRequestBlocking
, a permission that allows extensions to block requests dynamically based on their content (which
its replacement
does not support). Adblockers basically need
webRequestBlocking
to function properly. Pretty convenient (cough cough) for a company that makes most of its revenue from ads to be removing that.
Anyway, with the phasing-out of MV2 pretty much done, now seems like a good time to talk about a bug in Chrome that I found and reported to Google in 2023.
The bug
let
webRequestBlocking
(and yes, adblockers) work in MV3.
I still consider it probably the funniest bug I've ever found.
Stop writing browsers in JavaScript
Yes, Chrome is written in C++. However, extensions are written in JavaScript, and the API functions they call look just like JavaScript functions, at least from the extension's point of view. But they aren't normal functions: they're special and do browsery C++ stuff through bindings. In theory, this should be safe.
But in the old days, Google decided it'd be a good idea to inject a bunch of JS files into pages that used Chrome APIs. These "extension binding modules" would initialize API functions and validate arguments before passing them to the browser.
(Note:
here's the codebase
of those files in 2016.)
Turns out running privileged JavaScript in user-controlled websites was not a good idea, because JS can often be manipulated by overriding global functions and prototypes. Since certain APIs like
chrome.runtime
exist on normal websites too, the extension bindings system led to multiple Universal XSS bugs back in 2015 and 2016.
Here's one
that allows any website to inject code into any other website. Truly crazy stuff. If only I weren't 8 years old back then... maybe I could have cashed in.
Anyway, Google learned from their mistake and moved most API bindings to pure C++. However, a couple of JS binding files still exist and are used today. For example, if a Chrome extension runs the following code, it'll hit a
JS loop
and hang infinitely: (as of July 2025)
chrome.permissions.contains({ permissions: { length: Infinity }})
Maybe you are wondering what this has to do with adblockers.
Remember how I said only a few APIs still use JavaScript bindings?
chrome.webRequest
is one of them.
The bug
This is how an MV2 extension would block requests to example.com:
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(() => {
return { cancel: true }
}, { urls: ['*://*.example.com/*'] }, ['blocking'])
It's the
'blocking'
part at the end that requires the
webRequestBlocking
permission, and therefore isn't allowed in MV3. Without it, the
cancel: true
does nothing.
So clearly adding a blocking listener to the
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest
event does not work anymore. But we can do something crazy. We can make
our own event.
Now, this should not be possible; it's not even a concept that makes sense. But, because of how the JS bindings work, you can do it. For some reason, there is a
wrapper class
for
webRequest
events that contains some extra state.
(A
note on the security
of the above code.)
Instead of doing pure bindings between JS and C++, the browser creates one of these classes for every
chrome.webRequest
event:
onBeforeRequest
,
onCompleted
, etc. Surprisingly, the
.constructor
of these events is still public. It points to yet another wrapper class, which internally calls
WebRequestEventImpl
(from the code above). You can use this to can create a new event with your own properties:
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
let fooEvent = new WebRequestEvent("foo")
There is still a lot of validation going on in the backend when you try to actually do things with these fake events. For example, trying to add a listener to
fooEvent
kills the extension's process, because the event name is invalid. So how do you manipulate the properties of
WebRequestEventImpl
to do anything interesting?
After a lot of time looking into the C++ code, I found exactly one vulnerable thing: the
opt_webViewInstanceId
parameter. This was set for Chrome platform apps, in order to let them manage their embedded websites (WebViews). Among other things, it let them use web request blocking to control navigation. Basically, if an event had a WebView ID, the permission check for
webRequestBlocking
would be skipped
. The issue was that the browser never verified that an event with a WebView ID actually belonged to a platform app. So an extension could spoof it, skip the check, and use the blocking feature.
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
// opt_webV

The
third edition of Automate the Boring Stuff with Python is now available for purchase or to read for free online
. It has updated content and several new chapters, but one chapter that was left on the cutting room floor was
"Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams"
. I present the 26-page rough draft chapter in this blog, where you can learn how to write Python code that records and plays multimedia content.
Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams
These days a smartphone is a portable film studio that fits in your pocket. The ability to not just readily view but also produce video has led to an explosion of video content easily accessible over the internet. There’s plenty of video and audio editing software available for users of all levels of sophistication. But if you have, say, a thousand video files that you need to automate reducing their volume by 50% and then extract thumbnail images, you don’t want to have to edit each of those files individually yourself. Similarly, you may want to record video, audio, or photos from a laptop’s webcam for some automated process too specialized for off-the-shelf software. Or maybe you’d just like your program to play a funny sound effect. In this chapter, you’ll learn how to control your computer’s microphone, webcam, and speaker hardware from Python and play multimedia files.
This chapter assumes you have already read Chapter 21 to learn the basics about how programs work with image data. Since video is just a series of images, many of the same concepts apply.
Audio and Video Data
First, you should have a reliable way to open and view video and audio files. Since its release over twenty years ago, the open source VLC Media Player application has been free of charge and the gold standard for multimedia players. Install the VLC Media Player from
https://www.videolan.org/vlc/
, which runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Mobile versions for Android and iOS are also freely available. VLC is far superior to any multimedia application that came with your computer.
While you may be familiar with audio and video files by their file extension such as
.mp3
or
.webm
, audio and video formats are split into container formats and codecs. A container format is a wrapper that contains metadata and the encoded video or audio data. MP4, AVI, MKV, and MOV are popular container formats. A codec (or encoding) is the compression algorithm used for the video or audio data. MP3, H.264, VP9, and AAC are common video or audio codecs. Not all applications and devices support all codecs.
The audio file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.wav
files - an uncompressed format that are widely supported by apps and libraries but tend to have large file sizes so they are often used for short sound effects.
.mp3
files - a popular compressed format often used for music and other lengthy audio.
.ogg
files - an open standard, compressed format that is less popular than
.mp3
but provides better compression and quality.
The video file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.avi
files - an older format that tends to have larger file sizes.
.mp4
files - a popular format that is widely supported by different software
.mkv
files - an open format that has many features but isn’t as widely supported as
.mp4
.
.webm
files - a more recent format based on
.mkv
that offers better compression and quality.
Common Video Sizes and Aspect Ratios
The aspect ratio is the relative size of a video or screen’s width to its height, often written as
width:height
. For example, 4:3 (4 pixels of width for every 3 pixels of height) was a common aspect ratio for 20th century computer monitors and standard-definition televisions in the broadcast TV era. Today, 16:9 is common for most laptop screens and high-definition televisions. More recently, the wider 19.5:9 aspect ratio is becoming common for smart phones. An aspect ratio that is wider than it is tall has a
landscape orientation
, while an upright aspect ratio that is taller than it is wide is called a
portrait orientation
.
Screen resolution
is the number of columns and rows of pixels that a laptop or mobile screen displays. It’s often written as
width
x
height
, such as 1280 x 720 or 1920 x 1080 (also written as 720p and 1080p, respectively). Your laptop’s screen often supports multiple resolutions that can be configured in your operating system’s settings. Videos have one size, though they can be scaled larger or smaller to fit a display or app window. While videos can have any size, they often match common screen resolutions so they can be viewed in
fullscreen mode
without disproportionate scaling.
Recording from Webcams and Microphones
The webcam and microphone you use for video chats can be accessed by Python scripts through the OpenCV, sounddevice, and wavio Python packages. OpenCV, the open computer vision library, is an advanced open source imaging library. To use it you must first you must install the mathematics and data science package NumPy by running

Pyhoff
Description
The pyhoff package allows you to read and write the most common
Beckhoff and WAGO bus terminals ("Busklemmen") using the Ethernet bus
coupler ("Busskoppler") BK9000, BK9050, BK9100, or WAGO 750_352
over Ethernet TCP/IP based on ModBus TCP.
Key Features
Supports a wide range of Beckhoff and WAGO analog and digital bus
terminals.
Very lightweight: no dependencies; compact code base
Easy to extend
Using standardized ModBus TCP.
Provides high-level abstractions for reading and writing data
from/to IO-terminals with minimal code
Usage Scenarios
Industrial test setups.
Research automation setups.
Data acquisition and monitoring.
Installation
The package has no additional decencies. It can be installed with pip:
pip install pyhoff
Usage
It is easy to use as the following example code shows:

pyhoff
.
devices

*
# connect to the BK9050 by tcp/ip on default port 502
bk
=
BK9050
(
"172.16.17.1"

Contributing
Other analog and digital IO terminals are easy to complement. Contributions are welcome!
Please open an issue or submit a pull request on GitHub.
Developer Guide
To get started with developing the
pyhoff
package, follow these steps:
Clone the Repository
First, clone the repository to your local machine using Git:
git clone https://github.com/Nonannet/pyhoff.git
cd
pyhoff
Set Up a Virtual Environment
It is recommended to use a virtual environment to manage dependencies. You can create one using
venv
:
python -m venv venv
source
venv/bin/activate
#
On Windows use `venv\Scripts\activate`
Install Dev Dependencies
Install pyhoff from source plus the dependencies required for development using
pip
:
pip install -e .[dev]
Run Tests
Ensure that everything is set up correctly by running the tests:
pytest

data.title: QRS: Epsilon Wrangling
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在实现大规模正则表达式时遇到的性能问题，特别是使用非确定性有限自动机（NFA）处理“ε-转换”（无输入转换）的挑战。作者回顾了NFA和确定性有限自动机（DFA）的区别，NFA允许状态在没有输入符号时进行转换，这对于实现如“*”、“?”等正则表达式构造是必要的。文章详细解释了ε-闭包的概念，即通过ε-转换能到达的所有状态，并说明了如何遍历NFA以处理输入符号。作者还提到在处理复杂正则表达式（如包含循环的表达式）时，计算ε-闭包可能导致无限循环和重复状态的问题，提出需要用“记录路径”的方法来避免这些问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正则表达式和DFA（确定性有限自动机）在代码简化和性能优化中的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• o11c认为，如果可以接受比正则表达式稍弱的功能，代码可以变得更容易理解。通过直接使用DFA而不是通过NFA（非确定性有限自动机），可以简化逻辑。他提到除了类似于/(AB)+|(AC)+/的复杂模式外，大多数情况下正则表达式都可以简化，且这种复杂模式在他的工作环境中非常罕见。
• 他提到之前在尝试用C语言实现高效哈希表时遇到困难，因此这次在拥有完全测试的原型之前，避免使用C语言。

补充讨论：
• o11c提到他当前项目的进展：逻辑代码有1.0KLoC（千行代码），注释有0.5KLoC，测试套件有4.4KLoC，在最近一次重构后有40%的测试失败。他特别指出，由于使用了Python中一些“ obscure programming features”（如循环、字符串、分支和函数），Python的表现非常缓慢，让他感到困扰。

争议焦点：
• 是否应为了代码的可读性和简化而放弃正则表达式的完整功能，转而使用DFA。
• 在实现过程中选择C语言还是Python，以及如何处理Python在特定情况下的性能问题。

in many months, partly due to a flow of real-life distractions, but
also I’m up against tough performance problems in implementing
Regular Expressions at massive scale
.
I’m still looking for a breakthrough, but have learned things about building and executing finite automata
that I think are worth sharing. This piece has to do with
epsilons
; anyone who has studied
finite automata will know about them already, but I’ll offer background for those people to skip.
I’ve written about this before in
Epsilon Love
. A commenter pointed out that the definition of “epsilon”
in that piece is not quite right per standard finite-automata theory, but it’s still a useful in that it describes how
epsilons support constructs like the shell-style “
*
”.
Background
·
Finite automata come in two flavors: Deterministic (DFA) and Nondeterministic (NFA).  DFAs move from state to state one input
symbol at a time: it’s simple and easy to understand and to implement.
NFAs have two distinguishing characteristics: First, when you’re in a
state and an input symbol arrives, you can transfer to more than one other state. Second, a state can have “epsilon transitions”
(let’s say “ε” for epsilon), which can happen any time at all while you’re in that state, input or no input.
NFAs are more complicated to traverse (will discuss below) but you need them if you want to
implement regular expressions with
.
and
?
and
*
and so on. You can turn any NFA into a
DFA, and I’ll come back to that subject in a future piece.
For implementing NFAs, I’ve been using
Thompson's construction
, where
“Thompson” is
Ken Thompson
, co-parent of Unix. This technique is also nicely
described by Russ Cox in
Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple And Fast
. You don’t need to
learn it to understand this piece, but I’ll justify design
choices by saying “per Thompson”.
I’m going to discuss two specific issues today, ε-closures and a simpler NFA definition.
ε-closures
·
To set the stage, consider this regexp:
A?B?C?X
It should match “X” and “BX” and “ACX” and so on, but not “CAX” or “XX”.
Thompson says that you implement
A?
with a
transition to the next state on “A” and another ε-transition to that next state; because if you see an “A” you should transition,
but then you can transition anyhow even if you don’t.
The resulting NFA looks like this:
In finite-automaton
math, states are usually represented by the letter “q” followed by a number (usually italicized and subscripted, like
q
0
, but not here, sorry). Note
q4
’s double circle which means it’s
a goal state, i.e. if we get here we’ve matched the regexp.
I should add that this was produced with
draw.io
, which seems to make this sort of thing easy.
Back to that NFA
·
So, here’s a challenge: Sketch out the traversal code in your head. Think about the input strings “AX” and “BCX” and just “X”
and how you’d get through the NFA to the Q4 goal state.
The trick is what’s called the ε-closure. When you get to a state, before you look at the next input symbol, you have to set
up to process it. In this case, you need to be able to transition on an A or B or C. So what you do is pull together the
start state
q0
and also any other states you can reach from there through ε-transitions. In this case, the ε-closure
for the start state is
{q0, q1, q2, q3}
.
Suppose, then, that you see a “B” input symbol. You apply it to all the states in the ε-closure. Only
q1
matches,
transitioning you to
q2
. Before you look at the next input symbol, you compute the ε-closure for
q2
, which turns
out to be
{q2, q3}
. With this ε-closure, you can match “C” or “X”. If you get a “C”, you”ll step to
q3
, whose ε-closure is just itself, because “X” is the only path forward.
So your NFA-traversal algorithm for one step becomes something like:
Start with a list of states.
Compute the ε-closure of that list.
Read an input symbol.
For each state in the ε-closure, see if you can traverse to another state.
If so, add it to your output list of states.
When you’re done, your output list of states is the input to this algorithm for the next step.
Computation issues
·
Suppose your regular expression is
(A+BC?)+
. I’m not going to sketch out the NFA, but just looking at it tells
you that it has to have loopbacks; once you’ve matched the parenthetized chunk you need to go back to a state where you can
recognize another occurrence.
For this regexp’s NFA, computing the ε-closures can lead you into an infinite loop. (Should be obvious, but I didn’t realize it until
after the first time it happened.)
You can have loops and you can also have dupes. In practice, it’s not that uncommon for a state to have more than one
ε-transition, and for the targets of these transitions to overlap.
So you need to watch for loops and to dedupe your output. I think the only way to avoid this is with a cookie-crumbs
“where I’ve been” trail, either as a list or a hash table.

44514559.article_summary: 文章讨论了在实现大规模正则表达式时遇到的性能问题，特别是使用非确定性有限自动机（NFA）处理“ε-转换”（无输入转换）的挑战。作者回顾了NFA和确定性有限自动机（DFA）的区别，NFA允许状态在没有输入符号时进行转换，这对于实现如“*”、“?”等正则表达式构造是必要的。文章详细解释了ε-闭包的概念，即通过ε-转换能到达的所有状态，并说明了如何遍历NFA以处理输入符号。作者还提到在处理复杂正则表达式（如包含循环的表达式）时，计算ε-闭包可能导致无限循环和重复状态的问题，提出需要用“记录路径”的方法来避免这些问题。
44514559.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正则表达式和DFA（确定性有限自动机）在代码简化和性能优化中的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• o11c认为，如果可以接受比正则表达式稍弱的功能，代码可以变得更容易理解。通过直接使用DFA而不是通过NFA（非确定性有限自动机），可以简化逻辑。他提到除了类似于/(AB)+|(AC)+/的复杂模式外，大多数情况下正则表达式都可以简化，且这种复杂模式在他的工作环境中非常罕见。
• 他提到之前在尝试用C语言实现高效哈希表时遇到困难，因此这次在拥有完全测试的原型之前，避免使用C语言。

补充讨论：
• o11c提到他当前项目的进展：逻辑代码有1.0KLoC（千行代码），注释有0.5KLoC，测试套件有4.4KLoC，在最近一次重构后有40%的测试失败。他特别指出，由于使用了Python中一些“ obscure programming features”（如循环、字符串、分支和函数），Python的表现非常缓慢，让他感到困扰。

争议焦点：
• 是否应为了代码的可读性和简化而放弃正则表达式的完整功能，转而使用DFA。
• 在实现过程中选择C语言还是Python，以及如何处理Python在特定情况下的性能问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络年龄验证法律的合理性、实施方式及其对社会和个人自由的影响

不同观点：
• al_borland：认为年龄验证法律过度干预个人隐私，尤其是将身份验证交给第三方网站处理存在安全隐患。建议参考Apple Pay的生物识别技术进行年龄验证，避免泄露个人信息。
• poly2it：从个人经历出发，认为过度的数字监督和年龄验证限制了青少年的个人发展，尤其是对计算机和编程有浓厚兴趣的孩子。法律可能重蹈覆辙，进一步束缚青少年的数字自由。
• ViktorRay：指出文章对最高法院裁决的解读有误，裁决仅适用于淫秽色情内容，不包括艺术作品中的性场景或一般性内容。并解释了判断淫秽内容的“我一见即知”测试标准。
• everdrive：担心年龄验证一旦实施，可能会迅速扩展到所有网络活动，而不仅仅限于色情内容，从而威胁到自由互联网的存在。
• root_axis：关注法律的跨州执法问题，认为即便可能性不大，但某些州可能会积极执行，尤其在法官个人对某些内容感到冒犯时。
• _bent：认为过去30年没有严格的年龄验证并未造成明显负面影响，孩子们接触成人内容并不会导致严重后果。建议保持内容推荐，但不应强制执行。
• xp84：认为网络不应与现实世界有不同规则，建议寻找隐私保护的解决方案，而非仅仅反对变革。指出网络已成为生活必需品，单靠家长控制难以实现。
• landl0rd：作为保守派基督徒，虽然不支持所有年龄验证法律，但理解限制色情内容传播的动机。认为家长应承担教育责任，而非完全依赖国家管控。
• perihelions：将美国的现状与中国道德警察对比，表达对美国快速堕落至类似状态的担忧。
• soulofmischief：呼吁工程师抵制并反抗年龄验证法律，保护发表自由。
• spacechild1：批评田纳西州的法律对裸体的过度苛刻，认为这是美国清教主义的体现，且对裸体和暴力的双重标准不合理。
• tolerance：以讽刺口吻指出，若色情内容对某些人极其重要，他们应愿意为其奋斗甚至牺牲。
• M95D：提出技术解决方案，建议使用HTML标签标注成人内容，由操作系统或浏览器根据 parental controls 自动识别和处理，避免整个网站被屏蔽。
• VerdisQuo5678：对如何应对年龄验证法律表示困惑，尤其在英国类似的法律已通过的情况下，并提到可能通过生成虚假内容来规避法律。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于年龄验证法律是否侵犯个人隐私以及如何有效实施，同时平衡网络自由和未成年人保护。
• 讨论还涉及到家长责任与国家管控之间的界限，以及对色情内容和暴力内容的双重标准问题。
• 技术解决方案被多次提及，如生物识别技术和HTML标签，作为可能的折中方案。

data.title: 'Starter packs' have played a central role in Bluesky's rapid growth
data.author: FinnKuhn
data.article_summary: 新研究揭示了Bluesky如何利用“ starter packs”克服新社交媒体平台的冷启动问题，迅速扩大用户群。这些starter packs由平台用户创建，旨在快速建立或重建社区。研究发现，虽然只有6.25%的用户参与starter packs，但他们获得了显著更多的关注，并发布了更多内容。这种机制在高峰期贡献了高达43%的关注行为，但也加剧了用户间的人气不平等。此外，starter packs在真实事件引发的迁移浪潮中，帮助新用户迅速建立社交连接，但也存在被滥用于骚扰或付费加入高曝光包的风险。研究建议平台设计者和政策制定者利用这一策略创建更公平和可信的在线空间。

不同观点：

• [pnw] 对Bluesky的使用情况表示担忧，引用数据表明Bluesky的用户指标在过去一年中下降了10%到20%，暗示平台可能在走下坡路。
• [PaulKeeble] 提到Bluesky的转移扩展工具，可以帮助用户找到他们在Twitter上关注的相同用户，从而方便地在新平台上重建社交网络。
• [sandspar] 担心这种低摩擦的跟随机制会导致"富者愈富"的动态，并可能导致信息茧房效应，使得用户看到的内容趋同，减少了意外发现有趣内容的机会。
• [zzzeek] 引用TechCrunch的文章，指出Threads在用户数量上迅速追赶X平台，而Bluesky则在用户增长上几乎无变化，暗示Bluesky在竞争中处于不利地位。
• [hombre_fatal] 支持引入简便的方式探索完全不同的信息流，提到自己通过创建新账号来打破信息茧房，但认为这种方法麻烦且重复，希望能有一个更便捷的解决方案。
• [moomoo11] 表示对这类社交应用不感兴趣，认为自己并不在乎别人的看法或言论，并表示Hacker News已经足够满足其需求。

补充讨论：

• 用户增长和平台竞争也是讨论的焦点，部分用户对Bluesky的用户增长停滞表示担忧，并与其他平台进行比较。
• 不同用户对社交应用的使用动机和期望存在明显差异，有的用户积极探索新功能和信息，有的用户则对这类应用缺乏兴趣。

44544388.article_content:
back to list
Picture: Patrick Bal
‘Starter Packs’ facilitate growth on social media platforms.
Launching new social media platforms is notoriously difficult, as users risk leaving familiar content and, most importantly, their established connections. This challenge has reinforced the dominance of existing platforms.
However, new research, led by computer scientists at Lancaster University, TU Darmstadt and City St George's, University of London, reveals how Bluesky overcame this barrier using starter packs – an onboarding feature that helped Bluesky address the “cold start” problem and rapidly grow its user base.
“Vital onboarding strategy for the emerging social media systems”
“Our findings go beyond Bluesky: they point to a new framework for launching successful social platforms,” said Dr Onur Ascigil, Lecturer in Computer Science at Lancaster University and Principal Investigator of the study. “Starter packs are becoming a vital onboarding strategy for the emerging social media systems that are seeking to attract users from dominant platforms.” The researchers believe their findings could help platform designers and policymakers promote more equitable and trustworthy online spaces.
Starter packs can be created by anybody on the platform and generally aim to rapidly create new, or recreate existing, communities. Starter packs were adopted rapidly by Bluesky users, with more than 335,000 created in the first six months of their launch, the researchers found. They accounted for up to 43% of people following others in Bluesky during peak periods, and contributed to nearly 20% of all follow relationships across the full study period, from June 2024 to January 2025. Users included in starter packs received up to 85% more followers and posted 60% more than similar users not included.
“While only 6.25% of users were members of a starter pack at the time of the study, the outsized impact of these starter packs highlights how a relatively small mechanism can significantly influence network formation and user visibility,” said Dr Ascigil. However, the researchers also found that starter packs tend to reinforce existing communities rather than create new ones. They help users with already-large followings grow even more. The researchers say this raises concerns about deepening popularity inequalities.
Study also highlights risks
“Starter packs quickly became central to Bluesky’s network of social connections,” said
Leonhard Balduf
of TU Darmstadt, co-lead author of the study.
Saidu Sokoto, also a co-lead author from City St George's, University of London, said: “We also observed risks, such as reinforcing popularity gaps and enabling misuse, including harassment or pay-for-inclusion practices. There was anecdotal evidence that some users may be paying to be added to high-visibility starter packs.”
The study also tracked spikes in Bluesky’s growth that aligned with real-world events like the US elections and changes at X (formerly Twitter). The researchers say starter packs played a crucial role during these waves of migration, helping newcomers quickly establish social connections. “During peak migration periods—corresponding to the 2024 US elections and Twitter/X’s controversial decision to make content visible to users who had been blocked—between 20% and 40% of daily follow actions came from one-click starter pack follows,” said Dr Ascigil.
Starter pack themes analysed
Using machine learning, the researchers analysed starter pack themes and found the largest communities centred around art, politics, gaming, sports, and activism. Many starter pack members were public figures such as journalists, politicians, and activists, i.e., groups that tend to rebuild influence early on emerging platforms.
The study, Bootstrapping Social Networks: Lessons from Bluesky Starter Packs, will be presented at the
International Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM)
in Copenhagen this June.
The study’s authors are: Leonhard Balduf and Björn Scheuermann of TU Darmstadt; Saidu Sokoto, Andrea Baronchelli and Michal Krol of City St George’s University of London; Ignacio Castro of Queen Mary University of London; Gareth Tyson of Queen Mary University of London and Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; George Pavlou of University College London and Onur Ascigil of Lancaster University.
The study
Balduf, Leonhard et al.:
„Bootstrapping Social Networks: Lessons from Bluesky Starter Packs“
, Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media Vol. 19 (2025)

https://doi.org/10.1609/icwsm.v19i1.35810

• [sandspar] 担心这种低摩擦的跟随机制会导致"富者愈富"的动态，并可能导致信息茧房效应，使得用户看到的内容趋同，减少了意外发现有趣内容的机会。
• [zzzeek] 引用TechCrunch的文章，指出Threads在用户数量上迅速追赶X平台，而Bluesky则在用户增长上几乎无变化，暗示Bluesky在竞争中处于不利地位。
• [hombre_fatal] 支持引入简便的方式探索完全不同的信息流，提到自己通过创建新账号来打破信息茧房，但认为这种方法麻烦且重复，希望能有一个更便捷的解决方案。
• [moomoo11] 表示对这类社交应用不感兴趣，认为自己并不在乎别人的看法或言论，并表示Hacker News已经足够满足其需求。

补充讨论：
• 信息茧房和观点多样性是讨论的核心问题，部分用户希望通过技术手段打破信息茧房，获取更多元的信息。
• 用户增长和平台竞争也是讨论的焦点，部分用户对Bluesky的用户增长停滞表示担忧，并与其他平台进行比较。
• 不同用户对社交应用的使用动机和期望存在明显差异，有的用户积极探索新功能和信息，有的用户则对这类应用缺乏兴趣。

data.title: I Messed Up My Google PM Vibe Coding Interview
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI角色面试中的"vibe coding"及其相关争议

不同观点：
• [abxyz] 认为，发帖者（OP）在AI角色面试中遇到"vibe coding"是意料之外的，因为发帖者没有准备好展示这项技能，而不是对角色本身涉及编码感到惊讶。这与一般认为的项目经理（PM）面试中的"vibe coding"情境不同。
• [cavisne] 对帖子的真实性提出质疑，认为大科技公司的面试通常结构严密，招聘人员应明确说明评估内容，因此猜测这可能是个虚假帖子。
• [Incipient] 对"vibe coding"的实际工具链表示好奇，并提到目前使用的开发工具（如VSCode的编辑模式）虽然提高效率，但可能影响代码质量和可扩展性。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为谷歌可能在节省成本，通过雇佣一个能处理多项任务的PM来替代单独的PM和开发人员，反映出当前行业趋势。
• [BSOhealth] 指出，科技行业的角色（如PM、UX/设计等）将在未来融合，并怀疑帖子的真实性，认为大科技公司的面试通常足够结构化，不应出现这种意外。
• [Myrmornis] 认为发帖者并没有进行"vibe coding"，而是尝试实现一个代理，并指出"vibe coding"应在代理存在的前提下进行。
• [tra3] 认为即使发帖者在面试中感到失败，面试官应能透过压力看到所展示的技能。
• [jekwoooooe] 对"vibe coding"产生的应用持负面态度，认为这些应用在生产环境中会崩溃。
• [polotics] 提到曾签署保密协议，与此类话题相关。
• [alshival] 建议不要为大科技公司工作，认为这些公司对员工不重视，并分享了自己在教育和医疗行业工作的积极经验。
• [growbell_social] 认为"vibe coding"将成为许多角色的标准，并预测这是未来的趋势。
• [sunaookami] 认为像这样的帖子在Reddit上很常见，质疑其真实性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于帖子真实性和"vibe coding"在AI角色面试中的合理性。
• 对"vibe coding"工具链和实际效果的讨论，反映出对新技术和工作方式的不同看法。
• 对大科技公司招聘实践和工作文化的批评与辩护。
• 不同行业工作经验的比较，强调了在非科技行业工作的优势。
• 对未来工作角色和技能融合的预测和接受程度。

data.title: Show HN: Vibe Kanban – Kanban board to manage your AI coding agents
data.author: louiskw
data.article_summary: Vibe Kanban 是一个用于管理 AI 编码代理的看板工具。它可以帮助用户轻松切换不同编码代理、编排多个代理并行或顺序执行任务、快速审查工作并启动开发服务器，以及集中管理代理配置。安装时需要通过终端运行 `npx vibe-kanban`，并确保已认证编码代理。该项目使用 Rust 和 Node.js 开发，提供详细的文档和支持。用户可以通过 GitHub 提出问题和功能请求，但不建议未经讨论直接提交 PR。项目源码可在遵循 Apache-2.0 许可证下构建和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具及其在软件开发中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• [隐私和权限问题]
  ◦ [gpm] 指出该工具默认启用分析功能，收集用户的电子邮件和GitHub用户名，并跟踪各种开发活动，质疑这是否应得到用户的明确同意。
  ◦ [iimblack] 对工具要求的权限感到担忧，质疑一个看板工具为何需要访问代码和部署密钥。

• [工具的实用性和扩展性]
  ◦ [swalsh] 分享了自己构建类似工具的经验，指出在规模化时会出现复合误报的问题，并强调需要手动确认模型识别的潜在问题。
  ◦ [oc1] 提议在软件开发中引入类似厨房 brigade 的角色分配系统，以提高效率。

• [AI在编码中的角色]
  ◦ [adastra22] 质疑AI编码代理是否真的在主导世界代码编写的趋势，并对过度抽象化开发过程表示怀疑。
  ◦ [barbazoo] 认为“人类工程师大部分时间用于规划、审查和协调任务”的说法过于宽泛。

• [用户体验和工作流]
  ◦ [lharries] 对工具的协作功能表示兴趣，询问是否会有托管版本以便团队协作，并提出对依赖性PR管理的改进建议。
  ◦ [uxamanda] 分享了使用GitLab的命令行工具“glab”与混合团队协作的经验。

• [工具的长远价值]
  ◦ [helsinki] 认为该工具目前提供的功能终端和Git工作树也能实现，质疑其对高级用户的吸引力。
  ◦ [deepdarkforest] 对过度依赖AI编码代理表示担忧，认为这种抽象化可能会引入噪音和草率，特别是在企业级代码中。

• [生产力和工作满意度]
  ◦ [skeeter2020] 幽默地提出了在使用AI工具极大提升生产力后如何利用空闲时间的问题。
  ◦ [notarobot123] 对长期使用这种工作流的感受表示好奇，询问这种工作方式是否可持续并令人满意。

• [市场竞争和未来发展]
  ◦ [_jayhack_] 认为这种项目对传统项目管理平台构成威胁，并指出像Linear、Monday、ClickUp等平台正在积极改善UX以适应人机协作。

补充讨论：
• [工具推荐和资源整合]
  ◦ [mahsima] 建议将该工具添加到相关的AI编码工具列表中，以便更多人发现和使用。

争议焦点：
• 该工具的隐私问题和权限要求是否合理。
• AI编码代理在软件开发中的角色和影响，特别是对代码质量和开发过程的影响。
• 该工具是否提供了足够的独特功能以吸引高级用户和企业用户。

Get 10X more out of Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Amp and other coding agents...
Overview
AI coding agents are increasingly writing the world's code and human engineers now spend the majority of their time planning, reviewing, and orchestrating tasks. Vibe Kanban streamlines this process, enabling you to:
Easily switch between different coding agents
Orchestrate the execution of multiple coding agents in parallel or in sequence
Quickly review work and start dev servers
Track the status of tasks that your coding agents are working on
Centralise configuration of coding agent MCP configs
You can watch a video overview
here
.
Installation
Make sure you have authenticated with your favourite coding agent. A full list of supported coding agents can be found in the
docs
. Then in your terminal run:
npx vibe-kanban
Documentation
Please head to the
website
for the latest documentation and user guides.
Support
Please open an issue on this repo if you find any bugs or have any feature requests.
Contributing
We would prefer that ideas and changes are raised with the core team via GitHub issues, where we can discuss implementation details and alignment with the existing roadmap. Please do not open PRs without first discussing your proposal with the team.
Development
Prerequisites
Rust
(latest stable)
Node.js
(>=18)
pnpm
(>=8)
pnpm i
Running the dev server
pnpm run dev
This will start the frontend and backend with live reloading. A blank DB will be copied from the
dev_assets_seed
folder.
Build from source
Run
build-npm-package.sh
In the
npx-cli
folder run
npm pack
You can run your build with
npx [GENERATED FILE].tgz

data.title: Eye blink frequency variation and executive function enhancement from exercise
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文研究了极轻强度运动对静息状态下自发眨眼率（rssEBR）和执行功能的影响。24名健康年轻人参与了10分钟的极轻强度骑自行车运动和休息对照实验。结果显示，运动后眨眼率没有显著变化，但眨眼率的变化与斯特鲁普任务表现的改善存在显著相关性。这表明，虽然极轻强度运动不会一致增加眨眼率，但运动引发的眨眼率变化可以预测个体执行功能的增强程度。因此，rssEBR可能作为预测运动对大脑健康和认知影响的非侵入性生物标志物。

Abstract
Background
Acute physical exercise, even at a very-light-intensity, potentiates prefrontal cortex activation and improves executive function. The underlying circuit mechanisms in the brain remain poorly understood, though we speculate a potential involvement of arousal-related neuromodulatory systems. Recently, our rodent study demonstrated that exercise, even at light-intensity, activates the midbrain dopaminergic neurons. Resting-state spontaneous eye blink rate is linked to brain-arousal neural circuits, and potentially to those modulated by dopaminergic system. We hypothesized that neural substrates linked to resting-state eye blink rate contribute to the cognitive impact of acute very-light-intensity exercise.
Method
We analyzed data from a previous study with a renewed focus on resting-state eye blink rate. Twenty-four healthy young adults completed both 10 min of cycling (very-light-intensity exercise: 30% peak oxygen uptake) and rest conditions. Resting-state eye blink rate and Stroop task performance were measured before and after both exercise and resting control.
Results
Results showed no significant differences in eye blink rate changes between conditions. However, correlation analyses revealed that exercise-induced changes in resting-state eye blink rate were significantly associated with individual variations in Stroop task performance enhancement.
Conclusion
Very-light-intensity exercise does not elicit a consistent increase in eye blink rate after exercise. This finding does not support the involvement of a blink increase-linked neural substrate in enhancing executive function through very-light-intensity exercise. However, resting-state eye blink rate that is altered by exercise is predictive of executive function enhancement levels; this may serve as a novel contactless biomarker for predicting exercise benefits for brain health and cognition.

data.title: Russian use of chemical weapons in Ukraine is 'widespread' and growing
data.author: type0
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了欧洲情报机构指控俄罗斯在乌克兰广泛使用违禁化学武器，包括氯气和氯化苦（一种可致命的化学剂），以迫使乌军出洞并进行攻击。德国和荷兰情报机构指出，俄方的这种行为违反了《化学武器公约》。乌克兰及其支持者呼吁对俄实施更严厉制裁，并限制其参与国际组织。俄罗斯否认指控，反称乌克兰使用化学武器。此前，美国也曾指责俄方使用化学武器，但双方的指控均未得到充分证实。乌克兰方面报告了数千起与化学武器相关的伤害事件，局势令人担忧。

Russia

While it was already accused of using

Ukraine
, German and Dutch intelligence agencies say

has expanded its use of chemical weapons on the battlefield, including the use of potentially-lethal chemical choking agent chloropicrin.
Dutch intelligence said the chemical is dropped from Russian drones to force soldiers out of trenches so they can be shot, as Russia looks to continue making gains on the battlefield despite international efforts towards peace.
The chemical, which was widely used during World War One, can cause irritation of the lungs, eyes and skin and can cause diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea.

"The main conclusion is that we can confirm Russia is intensifying its use of chemical weapons," Dutch defence minister Ruben Brekelmans told Reuters, as he called for tougher sanctions for Moscow.
"This intensification is concerning because it is part of a trend we have been observing for several years now, where Russia's use of chemical weapons in this war is becoming more normalized, standardized, and widespread."
Germany’s BND foreign intelligence agency said Russia has been using not only tear gas but also "the more dangerous chemical chloropicrin, which can be lethal in high concentrations in enclosed spaces". This is a more serious violation of the Chemical Weapons Convention, it added.
European intelligence officials fear that Russia’s chemical weapons use is part of a large-scale intensification of chemical weapons production, and that Russian officials are issuing direct instructions to soldiers to use the poisonous warfare agents.
Russian chemical weapons use is “truly part of a large scale programme” rather than “some ad-hoc tinkering at the frontline”, said Peter Reesink, the head of the Dutch military intelligence agency (MIVD).
open image in gallery
The allegations come as Ukraine continues to face heavy air bombardment by Russian forces
(
REUTERS
)
The United States first accused Russia of using chloropicrin, a chemical compound more toxic than riot control agents, in May last year.
Kyiv has alleged thousands of instances of chemical weapons usage by Russian forces. The head of the Dutch Military Intelligence Agency (MIVD), Peter Reesink, noted "thousands of instances" of chemical weapons use, while also citing a Ukrainian figure of 9,000.
At least three Ukrainian deaths have been tied to chemical weapons use, Mr Brekelmans said, while more than 2,500 people injured on the battlefield reported chemical weapons-related symptoms to Ukrainian health authorities.
Moscow denies this, and has accused Ukraine itself of using such weapons. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on Wednesday that its security service discovered a Ukrainian cache of explosive devices in the east of the country containing chloropicrin. Kyiv has consistently denied such allegations.
The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), a disarmament agency in The Hague with 193 member states, said last year that initial accusations levelled by both countries at each other were "insufficiently substantiated".

data.title: Repasting a MacBook
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者试图为四年前的M1 Pro MacBook Pro更换导热膏以解决风扇噪音问题，但遭遇了一系列意外。起初，作者发现旧的导热膏已经干涸，计划用新的导热膏替换。然而，在拆解过程中，不小心弄坏了风扇电缆，之后又意外损坏了Touch ID传感器的电缆。文章解释了导热膏的作用和其随时间干涸的问题，并详细描述了拆解过程中的困难。最终，由于Touch ID传感器的加密配对特性，作者无法简单更换电缆，导致维修失败。作者建议普通用户不要轻易尝试自行更换MacBook的导热膏，以免造成不可逆的损坏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MacBook散热改造及维修难度

不同观点：
• [zdw] 提出在没有风扇的MacBook型号上，可以通过在CPU散热器和外壳之间添加导热垫，将整个底壳变成一个大散热片，从而延长最大性能时间。缺点是外壳会变得很热，但可以通过加装硬壳保护套解决。

• [t1234s] 分享了个人经验，提到2012年的MBP易于拆卸和维修，而2017年的MBP则质量和维修难度都很差。同时质疑新款M3/M4 MBP是否在拆卸和换电池方面有所改善。

• [dclowd9901] 将散热改造后的感觉比作给汽车换油，认为虽然实际变化不大，但主观感觉设备变得更健康。

• [gruez] 警告称，使用普通PC导热膏可能会在几个月后导致性能下降，因为它们比笔记本专用的导热材料更容易“泵出”。

• [haiku2077] 强调不应在Mac上使用普通导热膏或导热垫，建议使用专门的TCRS Carbon Black，而不是更换新零件。

• [gdbsjjdn] 对“友好拆卸过程”与“高昂维修成本”之间的矛盾表示讽刺。

• [smallpipe] 对比ThinkPad和MacBook的维修难度，认为MacBook虽然性能好但维修性差。

• [moribvndvs] 认为笔记本不适合长期高CPU使用，建议使用台式机进行此类工作。

• [nottorp] 表示旧款MacBook更具可玩性，并分享了个人的旧款MacBook改造经历。

• [jeron] 认为文章更像是在劝阻用户不要重新涂抹导热膏，质疑5度的降温和100分的Cinebench提升是否值得。

• [dsego] 分享了最近清洁MacBook的经历，指出灰尘导致的风扇噪音问题，并计划更换电池和扬声器。

• [ksec] 质疑为何笔记本不默认使用PCM（相变材料）作为导热介质，认为成本增加有限。

• [pram] 提到当前MBP的风扇几乎不运转，且内部几乎没有灰尘。

• [dmsnell] 分享了自己多次更换导热膏的经验，并指出导热膏降解对设备性能的长期影响。

补充讨论：
- 维修难度和设备设计变化是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是旧款和新款MacBook的对比。
- 导热材料的选择和使用寿命是另一个值得注意的讨论点，不同用户对导热膏的效果和风险有不同看法。
- 主观感受与客观性能变化之间的差异在评论中也得到了体现。

44531569.article_content:
You should repaste your MacBook (but don't)
July 10, 2025
My favorite memory of my M1 Pro MacBook Pro was the whole sensation of “holy crap, you
never
hear the fans in this thing”, which was very novel in 2021.
Four years later, this MacBook Pro is still a delight. It’s the longest I’ve ever owned a laptop, and while I’d love to pick up the new M4 goodness, this dang thing still seems to just shrug at basically anything I throw at it. Video editing, code compiling, CAD models, the works. (My desire to update
is
helped though by the fact I got the 2TB SSD, 32GB RAM option, and upgrading to those on new MacBooks is still eye wateringly expensive.)
But my MacBook is starting to show its age in one area: it’s not quiet anymore.
If you’re doing anything too intensive like compiling code for awhile, or converting something in Handbrake, the age of the fans being quiet is long past. The fans are properly loud. (And despite having two cats, it’s not them! I clean out the fans pretty regularly.)
Enter the thermal paste
Everyone online seems to point toward one thing: the thermal paste on computers tends to dry up over the years.
What the heck is thermal paste? Well, components on your computer that generate a lot of heat are normally made to touch something like a copper heatsink that is really good at
pulling
that heat away from it. The issue is, when you press these two metal surfaces against each other, even the best machining isn’t perfect and you there’s microscopic gaps between them meaning there’s just air at those parts, and air is a terrible conductor of heat.
The solution is to put a little bit of thermal paste (basically a special grey toothpaste gunk that is really good at transferring heat) between them, and it fills in any of those microscopic gaps.
The problem with this solution is after hundreds and hundreds of days of intense heat, the paste can dry up into something closer to almost a powder, and it’s not nearly as good at filling in those gaps.
Replacement time
The logic board!
MacBook thermal paste isn’t anything crazy (for the most part, see below), custom PC builders use thermal paste all the time so incredibly performant options are available online. I grabbed a tube of Noctua NT-H2 for about $10 and set to taking apart my MacBook to swap out the aging thermal paste. And thankfully,
iFixit has a tremendous, in depth guide
on the disassembly required, so I got to it.
Indeed, that grey thermal paste looked quite old, but also above and below it (on the RAM chips) I noticed something that didn’t quite seem like thermal paste, it was far moreâ¦ grainy almost?
Spottiness is due to half of it being on the heatsink
It turns out, ending with my generation of MacBooks (lucky me!) Apple used a very special kind of thermal compound often called “
Carbon Black
”, which is basically designed to be able to bridge an even thicker gap than traditional thermal paste. I thought about replacing it, but it seems really hard to come across that special thermal compound (and do not do it with normal thermal paste) and my RAM temperatures always seemed fine (65Â°C is fineâ¦ right?) so I just made sure to not touch that.
For the regular grey thermal paste, I used some cotton swabs and isopropyl alcohol to remove the dried up existing thermal paste, then painted on a bit of the new stuff.
Disaster
To get to the underside of the CPU, you basically need to disassemble the entire MacBook. It’s honestly not that hard, but iFixit warned that the fan cables (which also need to be unclipped) are incredibly delicate. And they’re not wrong, seriously they have the structural integrity of the half-ply toilet paper available at gas stations.
So, wouldn’t you know it, I moved the left fan’s cable a bit too hard and it completely tore in half. Gah.
I found a replacement fan online (yeah you can’t just buy the cable, need a whole new fan) and in the meantime I just kept an eye on my CPU thermals. As long as I wasn’t doing anything too intensive it honestly always stayed around 65Â° which was warm, but not terrifying (MacBook Airs completely lack a fan, after all).
Take two
A few days later, the fans arrived, and I basically had to redo the entire disassembly process to get to the fans. At least I was a lot faster this time.
The fan was incredibly easy to swap out (hats off there, Apple!) and I screwed everything back together and began reconnecting all the little connectors.
Until I saw it: the tiny (made of the same half ply material as the fan cable) Touch ID sensor cable was inexpicably torn in half, the top half just hanging out. I didn’t even touch this thing really, and I hadn’t even got to the stage of reconnecting it (I was about to!), it comes from underneath the logic board and I guess just the movement of sliding the logic board back in sheared it in half.
me
Bah. I looked up if I could just grab another replacement cable here, and sure enough you canâ¦ but the Touch ID chip is cryptographically paired to your MacBook

• [ksec] 质疑为何笔记本不默认使用PCM（相变材料）作为导热介质，认为成本增加有限。

• [pram] 提到当前MBP的风扇几乎不运转，且内部几乎没有灰尘。

• [dmsnell] 分享了自己多次更换导热膏的经验，并指出导热膏降解对设备性能的长期影响。

补充讨论：
- 维修难度和设备设计变化是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是旧款和新款MacBook的对比。
- 导热材料的选择和使用寿命是另一个值得注意的讨论点，不同用户对导热膏的效果和风险有不同看法。

data.author: cainxinth

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Bill Atkinson、Hypercard、以及 psychedelics（迷幻物质）的讨论，涉及历史、技术、社会接受度、安全性及合法化问题。

不同观点：
• notarobot123引用了Bill Atkinson的采访，指出Hypercard的灵感来源于一次LSD体验，将技术创新与迷幻体验联系起来。
• kmoser赞扬Bill的开放源代码方法使迷幻探索民主化，打破了昂贵静修和精英把控的限制，符合黑客精神。
• brainless表达了对迷幻物质的矛盾心理，虽然个人体验积极，但社会禁忌仍然存在，并对社会对其他有害物质（如糖、酒精）的接受度表示不解。
• dare944纠正了一个关于Bill Atkinson照片说明的错误，强调了General Magic这一Bill参与的项目，认为其未被广泛理解和欣赏。
• franze提到自己曾使用相同图片用于Atkinson Dithering Algorithm的学习页面。
• solfox强调初次体验迷幻物质时需要有经验的指导者，以确保安全和整合体验，认为这与首次接触计算机不同。
• xeonmc以幽默方式询问哪里可以找到迷幻社区，意图为游戏角色取名。
• _fat_santa主张推动迷幻物质合法化，建议设立由专业人员指导的治疗诊所，确保安全和规范。
• bikamonki请求以简单方式解释DMT如何消解自我。
• esseph希望迷幻物质的研究继续，并引用了一项关于psilocin延长细胞寿命的发现。
• kragen讨论世界上最强大的迷幻物质是个人电脑还是5-MeO-DMT，倾向于前者。
• Euphorbium分享了关于n,n DMT的体验，认为蒸汽方式最方便。
• WillAdams提供了Hypercard技术背景的链接，并对Hypercard及其继任者Livecode的命运表示遗憾。
• demiters不赞成将 transcendental（超验）体验商品化，认为限制 access 可以过滤掉不认真研究物质的人，减少负面结果的风险。
• hnthrowaway0315对迷幻物质的 unbiased research（无偏研究）表示怀疑，因其在加拿大非法，个人缺乏足够知识尝试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是迷幻物质的民主化与商品化之间的平衡，部分人支持更广泛的合法化和专业指导，另一部分人担心过度商品化会导致不良后果。
• 对迷幻物质的合法化和医疗化存在广泛讨论，有人提出设立专业诊所，有人则质疑社会对其他有害物质的接受度。
• 对迷幻物质的研究和安全性存在不同看法，有人引用研究结果支持其潜在益处，有人则对其合法性和研究充分性表示怀疑。

data.title: The great Malaysian cooking oil arbitrage
data.author: valkrieco
data.article_summary: 马来西亚的烹饪油补贴和欧盟的生物燃料 mandate 创造了一个套利机会：新鲜油可以低价购买、重新标记为“使用过的”油，然后高价卖给航空燃料生产商。根据《海峡时报》和《气候之家新闻》的报道，马来西亚马六甲出现了一个 scheme，当地人将烹饪油卖给那些供应欧洲航空燃料生产商的中介。欧盟要求航空公司使用更多来自可持续来源的生物燃料，而马来西亚政府补贴烹饪油，使得购买新鲜油便宜，转售“使用过的”油则有利可图。餐馆可以合法地通过使用几次后卖掉废油获利，但有人直接购买新鲜油而不使用，谎称是“使用过的”油，以赚取差价。这种欺诈行为动机明显且机会充足，马来西亚收集的“使用过的”油量惊人，人均远超其他国家。

44543781.article_content:
Malaysian cooking oil subsidies and EU biofuel mandates have
created
an arbitrage opportunity where fresh oil can be bought cheap, relabelled as 'used', and sold at a profit to aviation fuel producers.
...the Straits Times and Climate Home News recently reported on a striking scheme in Melaka, Malaysia, where locals were selling cooking oil that would eventually be used to supply European producers of aviation fuel.
The underlying idea of turning a waste product, used cooking oil, into something that can be blended into aviation fuel seems as appealing as
getting the cobras out of Delhi
. Cooking oil starts tasting bad after being used for frying three to five times, but as an input to aviation fuel, used oil is perfectly good.
At this point two intriguing forces intersect: European governments are demanding that airlines use more biofuels from sustainable sources — used cooking oil being one — while the Malaysian government subsidises cooking oil.
This means that in Malaysia buying fresh oil is cheap and selling used oil is lucrative. If you run a food stall or restaurant in Malaysia, you can buy subsidised fresh oil, fry food a few times, then sell the waste oil at a profit. It’s a nice side-hustle.
The trouble is, writes financial journalist Matt Levine, “If you don’t run a restaurant, you can buy fresh cooking oil for $0.60, not use it to fry food any times, and then say, ‘Oh, yeah we totally used this oil,’ and sell it to a refiner for $1.” That seems a simpler and more scalable way to proceed. It certainly cuts out the precarious, time-consuming hassle of actually running a restaurant. It is hard to know how much fresh oil is being resold this way, but fraudsters have both the motive and the opportunity.
Climate Home news notes that Malaysia collects an astonishing volume of “used” cooking oil: more per person than anywhere else, and two and a half times as much as second-placed Singapore.

data.title: Upgrading an M4 Pro Mac mini's storage for half the price
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者通过DIY升级套件将M4 Pro Mac mini的存储从512GB升级到4TB的过程。升级使用了M4-SSD提供的产品，总成本为699美元，远低于苹果官方的1200美元升级价格。升级过程相对简单，但需要小心拆卸后盖以避免损坏。由于采用 proprietary 接口，升级后必须通过DFU模式恢复系统。性能测试显示，升级后的内部存储在写入速度上优于外部Thunderbolt SSD，且更为稳定。尽管升级费用较高，但相比苹果官方选项仍具性价比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple SSD的性能、可升级性、价格以及数据完整性等问题。

不同观点：
• [dylan604] 认为SSD的速度非常惊人，相比过去的机械硬盘（HDD）阵列有显著提升，尤其是在视频编辑等实际应用中表现出色。他还提到过去需要多个设备和繁琐的操作才能达到现在的性能，而现在的SSD技术让工作流程更加高效。

• [GeekyBear] 指出Apple将SSD控制器集成到SOC（系统级芯片）中的一个重要原因可能是数据完整性。通过引用Apple收购Anobit的案例，说明Apple在NAND闪存的可靠性和寿命方面做了大量技术投资，以提升数据保存的稳定性。

• [Andrew_nenakhov] 批评Apple产品的存储和内存不可升级，并指出Apple对存储和内存的定价过高，例如32GB RAM/1TB版本的价格是16GB RAM/512GB版本的两倍，认为这种定价策略不合理。

• [radley] 分享了购买SSD后因过热问题而需要更换的经历，并提到卖家不提供保修，这使得购买高价SSD存在一定风险。

• [yread] 强烈批评Apple的4TB SSD价格过高，认为这是不合理的溢价。

• [dewey] 支持DIY升级，认为通过自行升级可以大幅节省成本，并且操作相对简单、可逆，性价比高。

• [gandalfian] 提到Apple产品的硬件限制（如5400rpm硬盘）对性能的影响，并通过自行更换NVMe SSD显著提升了设备性能，但也对Apple的产品设计表示不满。

• [Zenst] 讨论了可更换存储和焊接升级之间的差异，认为可更换存储更安全，而焊接升级的风险较高，需要专业技术。

• [zwilliamson] 提出使用其他品牌和操作系统（如Beelink SER8和Arch Linux + Wayland）作为Apple产品的替代方案，认为这样可以大幅节省成本并获得更高的可定制性。

• [gpm] 认为外部SSD在性价比和灵活性方面更具优势，特别是在不需要极高速度的场景下，外部SSD是更好的选择。

• [porphyra] 提到中国的一些店铺提供Mac mini的SSD升级服务，价格更便宜且包括DFU恢复等操作。

• [wpm] 强烈批评Apple在存储和内存方面的定价策略，认为这是不合理的“抢劫”，并指出Apple过去允许用户自行升级硬件，而现在则通过硬件限制和过高定价迫使消费者支付额外费用。

• [bee_rider] 对Apple产品命名中的“M”系列芯片名称提出疑问，认为命名不够清晰，容易引起混淆。

• [ProllyInfamous] 分享了自己使用四个4TB SATA驱动器和Terramaster外部硬盘盒构建16TB外部SSD RAID0的经历，认为这种DIY方案在性价比上优于购买Apple的高价SSD。

• [gigatexal] 认为为了节省时间和精力，直接支付Apple的“税”是值得的，因为时间比金钱更宝贵。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点主要集中在Apple SSD的高价和不可升级性上，部分用户认为这是不合理的定价策略，而另一些用户则认为可以通过DIY升级或外部SSD来解决。
2. 数据完整性和性能也是讨论的重要方面，尤其是Apple通过技术投资提升SSD可靠性的努力得到了部分用户的认可。
3. 不同用户对Apple产品设计和定价的满意度存在明显差异，一些用户强烈不满，而另一些用户则愿意支付额外费用以获得便利和性能提升。

44532306.article_content:
Upgrading an M4 Pro Mac mini's storage for half the price
A few months ago, I
upgraded my M4 Mac mini from 1 to 2 TB of internal storage
, using a then-$269 DIY upgrade kit from ExpandMacMini.
At the time, there was no option for upgrading the M4 Pro Mac mini, despite it
also
using a
user-replaceable
, socketed storage drive.
But the folks at
M4-SSD
reached out and asked if I'd be willing to test out one of their new M4 Pro upgrades, in this case, upgrading the mini I use at the studio for editing from a stock 512 GB SSD to
4 TB
.
I said yes, and here we are!
I documented the entire upgrade—along with taking my old M4 mini 1TB SSD and putting it in my
Dad's
M4 mini—in today's video:
But please continue reading, if you prefer text over video, like I do :)
The
upgrade process
itself is straightforward (if you've ever worked on laptop hardware before, at least), though removing the rear plastic cover (which also has the power button attached) is a bit annoying.
There are four metal pegs that are retained in clips in the bottom metal cover, and you have to slide a thin piece of metal / pry tool into the very minimal gap between the plastic bottom cover and the aluminum case, then pry it up. And if you're not careful on that step, you'll not only scratch the aluminum (and maybe crack the plastic bottom), but there's a good chance you rip the fragile (and tiny) power button connector too!
Besides that, it's a matter of removing a number of small torx screws; all the bits I needed were present in the cheapest iFixit assortment I have at my desk.
The only substantial difference between the M4 and M4 Pro mini SSD is the size and relative location—the M4 Pro has a much longer slot, a little more than a standard 2242-size NVMe SSD, while the M4 has a shorter slot, closer to a 2230.
DFU Restore
Speaking of standards... you
have
to do a full DFU (Device Firmware Update) restore, because unlike conventional M.2 NVMe storage, the M4 uses a proprietary connector, a proprietary-sized slot, and splits up the typical layout—the card that's user-replaceable is actually just flash chips and supporting power circuits, while the storage controller (the NVMe 'brains') is part of the M4 SoC (System on a Chip). Apple could use standard NVMe slots, but they seem to think the controller being part of the SoC brings better security... it certainly doesn't bring any cost savings, resiliency in terms of quick recovery from failure in the field, or performance advantage!
Since DFU restore is necessary, in my earlier video, I suggested you need an Apple Silicon mac (M1 or later) as the other computer.
But I was corrected by my viewers, who mentioned you can use many Intel Macs as well—I believe as long as a T2 chip is present, you're good to go. Just connect to the
middle
Thunderbolt port on the rear of the Mac mini, then press and hold the power button while plugging it into AC power. The other Mac should pop up an 'Allow this device to connect?' dialog and then you can proceed to the
DFU process
from there.
As far as I'm aware, no Hackintosh or other computer can be made to do a DFU restore.
I've done three upgrades (two on M4 minis, one on an M4 Pro mini), and all three were easy. The second one, I thought I had an issue, but it was just a confirmation dialog that wound up
behind
the active window.
Performance
I decided to also use an external Thunderbolt 5 NVMe enclosure from M4-SSD along with my (rather expensive) 8TB Sabrent Rocket Q SSD, and do a performance comparison.
See the video at the beginning of this post for some more detail (like all the numbers from
AmorphousDiskMark
and
Blackmagic Disk Speed Test
), but here are the raw numbers for large file copy performance:
The upgraded 4TB module performed noticeably better in writes, likely because it has more flash chips on it to spread out the write activity. Reads were pretty close to the same, with minor variance in performance across different file sizes and access patterns.
The external TB5 drive was the laggard, but is still ridiculously fast (by my standards, editing 4K video). And it would likely be faster if I used a good PCIe Gen 4x4 drive (the Rocket Q is Gen 3x4).
But the internal storage on these Mac minis is very fast, and even better, very
consistently
fast. The external Thunderbolt drive would slow down briefly every minute or so, after 100+ GB were copied—and I verified both with
smartctl
and
my thermal camera
that the drive was not overheating.
This is likely due to the internal DRAM cache on the NVMe SSD not being able to keep up with the high transfer speeds over long periods of time.
Conclusion
I was provided the
$699 M4 Pro 4TB SSD upgrade
by M4-SSD. It's quite expensive (especially compared to
normal
4TB NVMe SSDs, which range from $200-400)...
But it's not nearly as expensive as Apple's own offering, which at the time of this writing is
$1,200
!
Further reading
Don't pay $800 for Apple's 2TB SSD upgrade

• [dewey] 支持DIY升级，认为通过自行升级可以大幅节省成本，并且操作相对简单、可逆，性价比高。

• [gandalfian] 提到Apple产品的硬件限制（如5400rpm硬盘）对性能的影响，并通过自行更换NVMe SSD显著提升了设备性能，但也对Apple的产品设计表示不满。

• [Zenst] 讨论了可更换存储和焊接升级之间的差异，认为可更换存储更安全，而焊接升级的风险较高，需要专业技术。

• [zwilliamson] 提出使用其他品牌和操作系统（如Beelink SER8和Arch Linux + Wayland）作为Apple产品的替代方案，认为这样可以大幅节省成本并获得更高的可定制性。

• [gpm] 认为外部SSD在性价比和灵活性方面更具优势，特别是在不需要极高速度的场景下，外部SSD是更好的选择。

• [porphyra] 提到中国的一些店铺提供Mac mini的SSD升级服务，价格更便宜且包括DFU恢复等操作。

• [wpm] 强烈批评Apple在存储和内存方面的定价策略，认为这是不合理的“抢劫”，并指出Apple过去允许用户自行升级硬件，而现在则通过硬件限制和过高定价迫使消费者支付额外费用。

• [bee_rider] 对Apple产品命名中的“M”系列芯片名称提出疑问，认为命名不够清晰，容易引起混淆。

• [ProllyInfamous] 分享了自己使用四个4TB SATA驱动器和Terramaster外部硬盘盒构建16TB外部SSD RAID0的经历，认为这种DIY方案在性价比上优于购买Apple的高价SSD。

• [gigatexal] 认为为了节省时间和精力，直接支付Apple的“税”是值得的，因为时间比金钱更宝贵。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点主要集中在Apple SSD的高价和不可升级性上，部分用户认为这是不合理的定价策略，而另一些用户则认为可以通过DIY升级或外部SSD来解决。
2. 数据完整性和性能也是讨论的重要方面，尤其是Apple通过技术投资提升SSD可靠性的努力得到了部分用户的认可。
3. 不同用户对Apple产品设计和定价的满意度存在明显差异，一些用户强烈不满，而另一些用户则愿意支付额外费用以获得便利和性能提升。

data.article_summary: 2025年6月，太阳能首次成为欧盟最大的电力来源，提供了创纪录的22%电力。根据智库Ember的分析，至少13个国家太阳能发电量创下新高，荷兰和希腊的太阳能发电占比分别超过40%和35%。核能是第二大电力来源，随后是风能、天然气和水电。煤炭发电仅占6%，创下新低，15个欧盟国家已无煤电。6月的热浪期间，太阳能帮助缓解了电网压力，避免了停电。气候变化加剧了高温，导致大量与高温相关的死亡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲可再生能源，特别是太阳能的发展及其面临的挑战

不同观点：
• [mrtksn]: 对太阳能技术感到兴奋，认为欧洲由于缺乏化石燃料，发展绿色能源并非选择而是必要。虽然不反对核能，但认为其建设周期过长。还设想了一个全自动的太阳能光伏板工厂，可以自行扩展并利用捕获的太阳能生产面板。

• [ricardo81]: 指出太阳能和风能的平准化发电成本（LCOE）最低，但由于公众缺乏认知以及政治信仰的分歧，这一事实并未普及。认为国家应奖励已经采用绿色能源的人，而不是支付边际价格。

• [Someone]: 强调文章标题用词不准确，指出太阳能只是在电力供应中占比最大，而不是整个能源供应中占比最大。

• [toomuchtodo]: 认为需要更多的储能技术来稳定可再生能源的波动。欧洲电网目前依赖于天然气、法国核能和挪威水电来平衡可再生能源的波动。

• [ethan_smith]: 指出太阳能尽管容量因子较低（约15-25%），但依然达到了 headline 所描述的成绩，这意味着安装容量可能是 headline 数字的3-4倍。

• [layer8]: 提到西欧经历了有记录以来最热的六月，这一气候现象可能与太阳能发电量的增加有关。

• [exiguus]: 提到德国的可再生能源占比约70%，并计划在2035年前淘汰化石能源，最后一座核电站已于2023年关闭。

• [bryanlarsen]: 认为这一结果是经过挑选的，不像加州那样全面，但仍是一个好的进展。

• [athenot]: 指出六七月太阳能发电量高是合理的，但在十二月情况会有所不同。认为多样化的能源生产是好事，没有单一的解决方案，太阳能、风能、核能、化石能源和水电都有其优缺点。

• [Theodores]: 认为欧洲缺乏本土能源，长期依赖进口石油、天然气、铀和煤炭。指出可再生能源的崛起部分是由于制造业外迁，且很多太阳能技术来自中国，欧洲并非技术领先者。还提到乌克兰危机后欧洲对能源安全的担忧。

• [dexterdog]: 认为标题应明确为电网电力，并质疑柴油仍是所有能源发电中的主要来源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及太阳能技术的潜力和限制，如其低容量因子、储能问题及与其他能源的互补性。
• 政治和经济因素对可再生能源发展的影响，如公众认知、政策奖励及能源独立性。
• 不同国家（如德国和英国）在可再生能源转型中的具体策略和进展。
• 全球化对欧洲能源和制造业的影响，以及对能源安全的担忧。

44533843.article_content:
E360 Digest
July 11, 2025
In a First, Solar Was Europe’s Biggest Source of Power Last Month
Solar panels in Zaragoza, Spain.
Fernando Tomás via Flickr
For the first time, solar was the largest source of electricity in the EU last month, supplying a record 22 percent of the bloc’s power.
At least 13 countries saw solar output hit a new monthly high in June, according to an
analysis
from energy think tank Ember. Solar amounted to more than 40 percent of generation in the Netherlands and 35 percent in Greece.
Nuclear was the second biggest source of electricity across the bloc, followed by wind, natural gas, and hydropower. Coal generated just 6 percent of electricity, a new monthly low. Fifteen EU countries are now coal-free, including Austria, Belgium, and Ireland, which
shuttered
its last coal plant last month.
Analysts say that the June surge in solar power
helped
Europe weather a brutal heat wave, which saw
temperatures
soar upwards of 110 degrees F (43 degrees C). Solar power was most abundant at midday, when there was the greatest demand for air conditioning, helping to ease strain on the grid and prevent blackouts.
“Heat waves will not go away – they will only get more severe in the future,” said Pawel Czyzak, an analyst at Ember. “Luckily, there is no lack of sunshine during heat waves.”
Last month was the
warmest
June on record in Europe, and scientists say that climate change played a key role in the heat wave, pushing temperatures to dangerous extremes. An
analysis
from Imperial College London found that warming was responsible for 1,500 of the estimated 2,300 heat-related deaths across Europe, meaning “the death toll was tripled due to the burning of fossil fuels.”

data.title: I'm done with social media – Or: why I have a blog now
data.author: anarbadalov
data.article_summary: 作者原本计划在2024年通过社交媒体积极推广自己的新书《A Body Made of Glass》，以增加成功的机会。这本书因体裁不易分类、主题个人化且作者并非该领域的知名专家，使得推广更加困难。作者参加培训、请教专业人士，并专注于Instagram和TikTok，制作大量视频，分享每一个小成就。然而，作者很快感到不适，不擅长面对镜头，视频制作耗时，且这种方式开始改变其对生活的看法，使其生活变得像为了拍摄而存在。最终，作者对这种自我推广方式产生厌恶，特别是当发现这些努力并未得到社交媒体算法的青睐时，感到沮丧并决定放弃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体的使用、其对个人生活和工作的影响、以及未来发展趋势

不同观点：
• stego-tech认为，当前技术行业的过度集中和消费端缺乏创新使得人们开始重新审视自己与技术的关系，更多人会选择根据自己的价值观做出决策，尽管这可能会导致一些冲突。这种趋势可能会促使更多人选择脱离某些技术产品，而不是全面反对技术本身。
• teekert指出，大型社交媒体平台（如Facebook）存在不尊重用户的行为，例如通过误导性邮件诱导用户重新登录，这种行为让人感到不适。
• kmarc认为，社交媒体上的“创作者”和“消费者”有不同的体验，创作者容易迷失在追求关注和模仿他人的过程中，而观看者则可能沉迷于这些内容，失去其他更有意义的活动时间。
• freeopinion强调，社交媒体的初衷是促进人与人之间的交流，例如分享个人生活动态。然而，大多数人将社交媒体平台用作新闻或娱乐服务，而非纯粹的社交工具。此外，优质的社交媒体服务可能需要收费，但不确定有多少人愿意为此付费。
• mattgreenrocks将社交媒体比作大型多人在线游戏，目标是积累关注和社交指标，而非真正解决问题或创造价值。他认为，社交媒体提供的是真实沟通和行动的苍白影子，人们应该追求更多真实的生活体验。
• mrtksn怀念早期的互联网，认为当前的互联网被盈利性内容和算法主导，但相信未来会有新的形式出现，使得非极端主义的高质量内容再次繁荣。
• shortn提倡使用RSS feeds来替代社交媒体平台的算法控制，认为这样可以更好地管理内容消费，并减少不必要的精神负担。
• TechDebtDevin分享了自己因在Instagram上看到暴力内容而产生的焦虑经历，决定暂时退出社交媒体，转向Mastodon和Signal等更安全的平台。
• anarbadalov指出，社交媒体并非推广书籍的可靠工具，许多作者在此方面未能成功，且社交媒体的剥削性动态使得作者更难从中受益。
• alexpotato为社交媒体辩护，认为尽管其有诸多缺点，但在职业网络和行业交流中仍然具有重要作用，特别是对于寻找相关社区和分享个人见解的人来说。
• techterrier选择放弃Instagram，转而创建个人网站来展示自己的爱好作品，尽管访问量不高，但感到满意。
• tiniuclx尝试用社交媒体推广音乐和应用多年未果，感觉平台上的算法内容淹没了真实的社交互动。
• game_the0ry假设，媒体制作将从社交媒体平台逐渐转向个人化（去中心化）平台，因为用户对平台及其算法的疲劳感和不信任感增加，创作者也面临平台的限制和货币化困难。

补充讨论：
• 社交媒体的初衷和当前使用方式的偏离：许多人将社交媒体用作新闻和娱乐工具，而非纯粹的社交工具。
• 平台算法对用户体验的影响：算法推送导致用户看到大量噪音和煽动性内容，用户对此感到疲劳。
• 创作者在社交媒体平台上面临的挑战：包括难以货币化和随时可能被封禁的风险。
• 未来互联网和社交媒体的发展趋势：一些人认为去中心化平台和个人网站将逐渐取代当前的大型社交媒体平台。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体的价值和危害：一些人认为社交媒体提供了重要的职业和社交机会，而另一些人则强调其带来的精神负担和负面影响。
• 去中心化平台是否会取代当前的社交媒体巨头：一些人看好去中心化趋势，而另一些人则未明确表态。

44532913.article_content:
I started last year with one clear goal: 2024 was going to be the year that I finally
did
social media. Regular posting, a content calendar, a strategy, a plan for growth — all of that. And yet I ended the year pretty certain that I never wanted to open those apps again, let alone post my photos and words to them. How?
My main motivation for wanting to conquer my long-held ambivalence about posting was because I had
a book
coming out in April 2024. I was very anxious about this, in part because
A Body Made of Glass
was not an obviously easy sell. There are a few reasons for that: it blends several genres in a hard-to-categorise way, it tackles a subject in which I am not a well-known or previously published expert, and it is highly personal. It had also, in quite a modest way, done well according to the nebulous pre-publication benchmarks that authors obsess over. It had attracted a "Big Five" publisher in the US, something I had not had before, received a BBC radio serialisation deal in the UK, and had received some decent early reviews from industry publications in both places. I felt I should be leaving no stone unturned to support the book's success, since I had been gifted opportunities that many other writers would love to have. Chances, too, that I may never have again.
There are very few things that an author can practically do to make a book a success, especially after said book is written, edited and printed. Being a celebrity or personality with a pre-existing audience that adores you definitely helps, but isn't something you can suddenly decide to become four months before your publication date. Catching a particular trend or moment that causes publishers to invest heavily in promotion and booksellers to place large early orders is great too, but once the book is done that's up to them, not you. Giving off that nebulous aura of "I'm about to become a huge literary success" that seems to cling to some people and not others would be good as well, but is also pretty hard to engineer deliberately if that's not your personality or presentation (and it isn't mine).
In that tense, quiet period after the book has been finalised but before anyone can buy or read it, augmenting your personal brand via the regular use of social media feels like the only concrete action you can take. Or at least it did to me, so I threw myself into it. I attended some training sessions on "social media for authors". I asked professional acquaintances with expertise for tips. I learned that Instagram and TikTok were the best platforms to target for bookish followers and that the algorithms of these platforms were, these days, only interested in vertical videos. I compiled lists of videos I could make and started filming mostly-daily updates about my experience as an author with a book coming out soon. I scoured the accounts of other authors who were more successful than me on social media for insights. I posted about every tiny bit of publicity my book got or small win I achieved. I asked people to pre-order in as many ways as I could think of. I delved into the analytics, searching for ways to optimise and improve. I spent a lot of time scrolling, and scrolling, and scrolling, hunting for the "one weird trick" that would help me make a success of this.
I quickly began to feel quite uncomfortable. I'm not a natural on camera and I don't have that talent for talking effortlessly and engagingly to a lens when alone in a room that successful social media personalities need. I was forcing it all the time, making myself record multiple takes and doing things again and again until they looked "natural" (a highly unnatural behaviour). My video editing skills are basic, so turning out regular videos took me a long time. Worst of all, though, was the way in which this enterprise began to alter my mindset about the normal stuff of life. I never used to think very hard about what I wore for a casual day of writing at home, or worry about how clean the bathroom mirror was, or obsess over what narrative or story might emerge from my general jumble of accumulated tasks. It shocked me how quickly I started viewing my own life as something to film and share, rather than something to just... live. I've seen this effect
described
as "the devil had taken my eyes" and I feel that is accurate. Something had taken over my gaze and it wasn't something good. A new and sinister lens had appeared between me and the world. One evening, as I made my husband walk our dog past the same scenic view multiple times so that I could get the best shot of it for a video, I experienced a sudden wave of revulsion for myself and what I was doing. From then on, I began to despise the way this supposedly necessary aspect of modern authorship was intruding on parts of me that I had never meant to be available for public consumption.
Worst of all, perhaps, it didn't even seem to be
doing
anything. The TikTok and Instagram algorithms were utterly disinterested in what
44532913.article_summary: 作者原本计划在2024年通过社交媒体积极推广自己的新书《A Body Made of Glass》，以增加成功的机会。这本书因体裁不易分类、主题个人化且作者并非该领域的知名专家，使得推广更加困难。作者参加培训、请教专业人士，并专注于Instagram和TikTok，制作大量视频，分享每一个小成就。然而，作者很快感到不适，不擅长面对镜头，视频制作耗时，且这种方式开始改变其对生活的看法，使其生活变得像为了拍摄而存在。最终，作者对这种自我推广方式产生厌恶，特别是当发现这些努力并未得到社交媒体算法的青睐时，感到沮丧并决定放弃。
44532913.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体的使用、其对个人生活和工作的影响、以及未来发展趋势

不同观点：
• stego-tech认为，当前技术行业的过度集中和消费端缺乏创新使得人们开始重新审视自己与技术的关系，更多人会选择根据自己的价值观做出决策，尽管这可能会导致一些冲突。这种趋势可能会促使更多人选择脱离某些技术产品，而不是全面反对技术本身。
• teekert指出，大型社交媒体平台（如Facebook）存在不尊重用户的行为，例如通过误导性邮件诱导用户重新登录，这种行为让人感到不适。
• kmarc认为，社交媒体上的“创作者”和“消费者”有不同的体验，创作者容易迷失在追求关注和模仿他人的过程中，而观看者则可能沉迷于这些内容，失去其他更有意义的活动时间。
• freeopinion强调，社交媒体的初衷是促进人与人之间的交流，例如分享个人生活动态。然而，大多数人将社交媒体平台用作新闻或娱乐服务，而非纯粹的社交工具。此外，优质的社交媒体服务可能需要收费，但不确定有多少人愿意为此付费。
• mattgreenrocks将社交媒体比作大型多人在线游戏，目标是积累关注和社交指标，而非真正解决问题或创造价值。他认为，社交媒体提供的是真实沟通和行动的苍白影子，人们应该追求更多真实的生活体验。
• mrtksn怀念早期的互联网，认为当前的互联网被盈利性内容和算法主导，但相信未来会有新的形式出现，使得非极端主义的高质量内容再次繁荣。
• shortn提倡使用RSS feeds来替代社交媒体平台的算法控制，认为这样可以更好地管理内容消费，并减少不必要的精神负担。
• TechDebtDevin分享了自己因在Instagram上看到暴力内容而产生的焦虑经历，决定暂时退出社交媒体，转向Mastodon和Signal等更安全的平台。
• anarbadalov指出，社交媒体并非推广书籍的可靠工具，许多作者在此方面未能成功，且社交媒体的剥削性动态使得作者更难从中受益。
• alexpotato为社交媒体辩护，认为尽管其有诸多缺点，但在职业网络和行业交流中仍然具有重要作用，特别是对于寻找相关社区和分享个人见解的人来说。
• techterrier选择放弃Instagram，转而创建个人网站来展示自己的爱好作品，尽管访问量不高，但感到满意。
• tiniuclx尝试用社交媒体推广音乐和应用多年未果，感觉平台上的算法内容淹没了真实的社交互动。
• game_the0ry假设，媒体制作将从社交媒体平台逐渐转向个人化（去中心化）平台，因为用户对平台及其算法的疲劳感和不信任感增加，创作者也面临平台的限制和货币化困难。

补充讨论：
• 社交媒体的初衷和当前使用方式的偏离：许多人将社交媒体用作新闻和娱乐工具，而非纯粹的社交工具。
• 平台算法对用户体验的影响：算法推送导致用户看到大量噪音和煽动性内容，用户对此感到疲劳。
• 创作者在社交媒体平台上面临的挑战：包括难以货币化和随时可能被封禁的风险。
• 未来互联网和社交媒体的发展趋势：一些人认为去中心化平台和个人网站将逐渐取代当前的大型社交媒体平台。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体的价值和危害：一些人认为社交媒体提供了重要的职业和社交机会，而另一些人则强调其带来的精神负担和负面影响。
• 去中心化平台是否会取代当前的社交媒体巨头：一些人看好去中心化趋势，而另一些人则未明确表态。

June 27, 2018
Series of posts on HTTP status codes
Because I want to get into the habit of blogging on a regular basis, I thought
it would be a fun idea to write a series of articles on one of my favourite
topics: HTTP and Webservices.
To start, I began writing an article for every HTTP status code. I only
realized after I drafted the first few, that the
IANA
page actually lists
68 official ones. Definitely a bit more than I thought, but I started and I’m
going to see if I can finish it.
I’m going to release the first few this week, and then switch to a weekly
schedule. Hopefully I can keep this going for a year!
Today I published the first one:
100 Continue
.
If you’re interested to read the future ones or want to show support, you can:
Subscribe to the mailing list
, which I’ve setup for this purpose.
Subscribe to my RSS feed
Or just follow me on
Twitter
.

data.title: LLM Inference Handbook
data.author: djhu9
data.article_summary: 《LLM Inference in Production》是一本技术手册，汇集了大语言模型（LLM）推理的核心概念、性能指标（如首 token 时间、每秒 token 数）、优化技术（如连续批处理、前缀缓存）及运营最佳实践。它旨在解决知识碎片化问题，帮助工程师更有效地部署、扩展和操作 LLMs。手册涵盖推理与训练的区别、goodput 对服务水平目标（SLOs）的重要性、以及 prefill-decode 拆分等实用内容。适合希望提升 LLM 推理速度、降低成本或提高可靠性的工程师使用。手册可从头到尾阅读，也可作为参考资料查阅，并将随着领域发展持续更新。欢迎通过 GitHub 提交问题或贡献内容。

不同观点：

• [subset] 对项目表示赞赏，并建议添加有关结构化输出和引导生成等内容，同时提供了一个关于采样算法的参考链接。
